title: Province stays out of police shooting probe
article: The province will not become involved at this stage in an investigation into the shooting of an Alert Bay woman by police, Solicitor-General Rich Coleman said Tuesday.

RCMP took the most appropriate action by meeting with the Alert Bay community about the death, he said. RCMP officers took part in a town hall meeting with about 200 residents to explain what happened.
"I think police are doing the right thing by going in to visit the community so they can put the facts on the table," Coleman said.
Coleman, a former RCMP officer, said it would be inappropriate to comment until the police investigation is completed.
"Police are asked to make split- second decisions that are difficult. Sometimes their lives are in danger and I would never second- guess anyone put into those circumstances," he said.
Lorraine Jacobson, 40, was shot dead after she ignored an order to put down a butcher knife.
The officer who shot Jacobson was responding to a domestic dispute at a home last Friday on the Whe la la U aboriginal reserve at the northern tip of Vancouver Island.
RCMP Sergeant Lee Omilusik said in a news release the officer, finding himself locked out of the house, was waiting for back-up when he saw a woman threaten a man inside with a butcher knife.
Someone then unlocked a door, allowing entry by the officer, who ordered the woman to drop the knife.
She refused and was shot once as she approached the officer, police said.
After the incident, reserve residents questioned why the officer had to shoot Jacobson.
